title: Right-additivity of the dot product over $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$
statement:
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a dimension $n$, and let $s, x, y \in (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n$. Writing $s \cdot x = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} s_i x_i \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ for the componentwise dot product, the dot product is additive in its right argument:
\[
s \cdot (x + y) = s \cdot x + s \cdot y,
\]
where $x + y$ denotes the componentwise sum.
hypotheses_covered: s, x, y are vectors over Z/kZ of length n
replaced:
For $s, x, y \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$,
$s \cdot (x + y) = s \cdot x + s \cdot y$.
